items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: And McGuire was the name of the boss there, McGuire.

ctx.x: All I remember is that it didn't last long, and we were so upset. I got my money, and whoever told us it was going to be a long run -- yeah, one week. Didn't have the correct backing. Now, Maxine's was a different place. Very nice. And when that closed, Maxine's closed, we went to City Island, at the Showboat, it was a place in City Island that we went to.

And McGuire was the name of the boss there, McGuire. And we played there for about -- oh, two or three months, I think. Yeah. That was nice. We used to drive out there every night. Now, during that time, television was beginning to sneak in, only rich people had it at that time because -- and the big bands, one by one, was starting to wake up, and nightclubs were starting to fold up. Because during that era when television came in, everything went out, all that live music.
